answer: An operator holding 146 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the signal balance is debited each close, the tundra ledger publishes the bleed, and the horizon audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 17% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
